parole.significato: A large mass or body of snow and ice sliding swiftly down a mountain side, or falling down a precipice.
parole.testo: From French avalanche, from Franco-Provençal (Savoy) avalançhe, blend of aval (“downhill”) and standard lavençhe, from Vulgar Latin *labanka (compare Occitan lavanca, Italian valanga), of uncertain origin, perhaps an alteration of Late Latin lābīna (“landslide”) (compare Franco-Provençal (Dauphiné)

parole.significato: An alpine style of wooden building with a sloping roof and overhanging eaves.
parole.testo: Borrowed from French chalet, from Franco-Provençal çhalè (“herdsman's hut in the mountains”).

parole.significato: A large body of ice which flows under its own mass, usually downhill.
parole.testo: Borrowed from French glacier, from Franco-Provençal gllaciér, from Vulgar Latin *glaciārium, a derivative of Latin glaciēs (“ice”), of uncertain origin. First attested in English in 1744 per the OED.

parole.significato: The firn or snowfield at the head of a glacier.
parole.testo: Borrowed from French névé, from the Franco-Provençal (Savoyard) term névi (“mass of snow”), from Latin nivatus "snow-cooled" (< Latin nix, nivis (“snow”)).
Borrowed from French piolet, or its source, Franco-Provençal piolet (“small axe”).
